kntx.tagline: Turning fight video into actionable tactical data.
kntx.description: An end-to-end AI platform for taekwondo fight analysis: experts annotate videos, I train my own models on that data, a video pipeline detects, tracks and classifies every action, then coaches review and correct the analysis. Every correction feeds the next training cycle.
highlights: My own models, trained on expert-annotated fights: multi-task BiLSTM (technique, target, role), fine-tuned MotionBERT Transformer, 1D CNN action spotter, benchmarked against graph networks (ST-GCN, CTR-GCN)
Computer vision: YOLO fine-tuned on 3 classes (blue fighter, red fighter, referee), BoT-SORT tracking, RTMPose pose estimation, homographic mat calibration and scoreboard OCR
Active learning loop: coach corrections retrain the model, which is only deployed after a quality gate (macro F1 on a frozen test set)
Tactical memory on pgvector: similar-action search from embeddings produced by my models and by Claude Haiku summaries (HNSW index, p95 of 16.5 ms over 100,000 vectors in a local benchmark)
LLM data analysis: athlete reports (Llama 3.3 via Groq) and metric suggestions (Gemini)
Desktop (Electron) and iPad (SwiftUI + Vision) annotation tools, GPU inference on Modal, GDPR consent for biometric data
kntx.visualAlt: AI analysis of a taekwondo fight: both fighters detected, with tracking IDs and pose skeletons

memotale.tagline: Memories told out loud become the book of a life.
memotale.status: Launching soon on the App Store and Google Play
memotale.description: You record a memory in your own language, Darija included. AI transcribes it, dates it, places it, then writes it faithfully, without inventing a single fact, and inserts it at the right point of a chronological book the whole family can read and add to.
highlights: AI transcription and writing, every sentence stays linked to the original recording
One continuous, chronological book: neighbouring transitions are rewritten with each new memory
Six languages including Darija, Arabic right-to-left UI and Chinese books
Private family sharing, free lifetime reading for relatives
Subscriptions through Apple In-App Purchase and Google Play Billing

momochee.status: Web live · iOS soon · Android early access
momochee.description: A family gamification platform: parents set the rules (chores, school, behaviour), children complete quests, grow their pixel-art creature and trade their points for real rewards.
highlights: Two experiences in one app: gamified for children, calm and efficient for parents
Pixel-art creature engine: 16 species, evolution, fusion into unique hybrids
AI homework correction from a photo, with a score and encouragement
Turborepo monorepo: Next.js 15 web app and REST API consumed by the Expo app
Stripe payments, push notifications, biometrics and family chat

babyiq.tagline: Every day is a chance to grow your baby's mind.
babyiq.status: Web app live · iOS and Android soon
babyiq.description: A flashcard app inspired by the Doman method for children aged 0 to 6. Sessions last a few seconds, several times a day: the app plans and rotates the cards, so the parent only has to press “Start”.
highlights: Offline-first sessions: showing cards never depends on the network
Dynamically generated quantity cards with no overlapping dots
Automatic card rotation and a daily plan for each child
No testing of the child, personal data kept to the bare minimum
Cross-platform subscription: Apple In-App Purchase, Google Play Billing and Stripe

services.title: What AI can do for you
services.lead: Everyone talks about “AI-powered” companies. Few people say what it concretely changes. Here are specific use cases I can analyse, prototype and integrate into your tools.
services.manifestoText: A language model is not a magic wand: poorly scoped, it makes things up, costs a lot and worries teams. Used well, it saves time on specific tasks, with results you can check.

docs.name: Document drafting
docs.today: Your teams spend hours writing, rephrasing and formatting documents from information that already exists.
examples: A recorded meeting becomes structured minutes, with decisions and assigned actions
Field notes become a standard operating procedure in your house style
A first draft of a tender response, built from your past answers and references
docs.impact: Teams review and approve instead of starting from a blank page, and documents become more consistent.
docs.guardrail: Every document is reviewed by a person before it goes out, and the AI only writes from your sources.

data.name: Data & cost analysis
data.short: Purchasing, stock, invoices: see where money goes
data.today: The data exists (ERP exports, invoices, spreadsheets) but nobody has time to cross-check it and spot drift.
examples: Supplier invoice analysis to spot duplicates, price gaps and unjustified increases
Detection of dormant stock and recurring shortages from historical data
Plain-language questions to your data, such as “Which suppliers raised their prices this quarter?”, with the calculation shown
data.impact: Savings opportunities surface regularly, quantified and verifiable, instead of waiting for a yearly audit.
data.guardrail: Calculations are done by verifiable code, not guessed by the model: AI is there to explore and explain.

automation.name: Task automation
automation.today: Copying data from a PDF into a spreadsheet, sorting emails, chasing customers: repetitive tasks that tie up skilled people.
examples: Data extraction from invoices, purchase orders or PDF forms into your ERP or spreadsheet
Sorting incoming emails (quotes, complaints, invoices) and routing them to the right person with a summary
Follow-ups and weekly reports prepared and sent automatically
automation.impact: Less re-typing, fewer copy errors, and time given back to teams for work that needs judgement.
automation.guardrail: Uncertain cases are flagged and approved by a person, and every action is logged.

rag.name: Assistant on your documents (RAG)
rag.short: Sourced answers drawn from your documentation
rag.today: The information is in your procedures, contracts or knowledge bases, but finding it takes time, and the wrong version circulates.
examples: An internal assistant that answers staff questions from your procedures, with a cited, clickable source
First-line customer support grounded only in your product documentation
Access rights respected: each person only gets answers from documents they are allowed to read
rag.impact: Answers arrive in seconds, always with their source, and experts are interrupted less for repetitive questions.
rag.guardrail: When the documentation does not contain the answer, the assistant says so instead of making it up.

agents.name: Specialised agents
agents.today: Some tasks take several steps (search, compare, qualify, write) and vary too much for classic automation.
examples: A monitoring agent that watches chosen sources (tenders, regulation, competitors) and sends you a summary
A qualification agent that enriches and prioritises incoming requests before a salesperson handles them
A file preparation agent that gathers documents, checks nothing is missing and prepares a draft
agents.impact: The preparatory steps are done, and your teams step in where their expertise matters.
agents.guardrail: A limited scope of action, visible steps and human approval before any committing action.

custom.name: Models trained on your data
custom.today: Some needs go beyond general-purpose models: analysing video, recognising movements or classifying data that is very specific to your business.
examples: Video analysis: automatically detect, track and classify movements or events, as I do for taekwondo fights
A classification model trained on your own annotated data, when a general-purpose model gets it wrong or costs too much to run
Similarity search across your history (similar cases, situations or parts) with embeddings and pgvector
custom.impact: A model specialised on your problem, running on your infrastructure and improving with your teams' corrections.
custom.guardrail: A frozen test set and a quality bar to clear before every release; uncertain cases are still approved by a person.

steps.title: Understanding your needs
steps.text: A conversation to understand your processes, spot repetitive or costly tasks and the data available. Together we define what success looks like.

steps.title: Measured prototype
steps.text: A first version on your real documents or data, tested on real cases, with criteria set in advance.

steps.title: Integration
steps.text: Production rollout into your existing tools, with security, access rights and GDPR compliance planned from the start.

steps.title: Follow-up & handover
steps.text: Measuring results, adjusting, and training your teams so they stay in control.

principles.title: My principles
items: Start from the need, not the tool.
If simple automation is enough, no AI needed.
Measure before and after, on real cases.
Keep a human in the loop for what matters.
Your data stays under control: access, hosting, confidentiality.

experience.title: Background

That field experience is an asset: I know the reality of processes, procedures and quality constraints, and I build tools for the people who actually use them. Taekwondo is my other field of expertise: KNTX Labs was born where the two meet.
